pages.heading: An Invitation to Global Leaders
body: We stand at the most critical crossroads in history. Artificial intelligence is reshaping the course of civilization — surpassing any revolution that came before.
Yet the most critical question for humanity remains not: "How powerful will AI become?" But rather: "Do humans still remember the purpose for which God created us?"
Technology can expand human capabilities, but it cannot create love; it can generate information, but it cannot generate wisdom; it can connect the world, but it cannot heal the human heart.

Our declaration: Technology may change the speed of the world, but only Truth determines its direction. AI can expand human capability, but it can never replace human dignity or divine destiny. The greatest crisis of the future is not that AI becomes too powerful — it is that humanity loses heaven's wisdom.
We sincerely invite pastors, innovators, educators, business leaders, media pioneers, and next-generation influencers to join this historic gathering.

Together we will explore: Faith & Artificial Intelligence, Future Church Leadership, Digital Civilization & Biblical Stewardship, Global Kingdom Collaboration, the Rising Influence of Asia, and the Future & Hope of Humanity.
The future does not belong to machines — but to leaders who carry wisdom, character, courage, and the love of Christ.
"Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD rises upon you." — Isaiah 60:1

items.v: At the heart of Arizona in the American Southwest — the state's capital and center of government and commerce.
Set in the Sonoran Desert's "Valley of the Sun," where the city weaves together with surrounding mountains and desert preserves.
Fly into Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX); about 15–25 minutes by car to the summit venue in Tempe.
TSMC has announced $165 billion in investment and 6 planned fabs, earning Phoenix the nickname "Desert Silicon Valley."
Population of roughly 1.7 million — the 5th largest city in the USA.

pages.heading: First Baptist Church of Tempe
body: First Baptist Church of Tempe was founded in 1887 and carries over a century of history. Grounded in the truth of Scripture as the core of its faith and teaching, the church holds "Love God, Love People" as its mission — devoted to discipleship, biblical education, missions, and community service.

For more than a hundred years, the church has equipped believers across generations through diverse ministries, living out faith and sharing the gospel in daily life and community, united by the shared goal of "glorifying God in all things."
